About the Evening

When the sun softens, we show up.

August is National Black Business Month. When the sun begins its descent over the Eastside on August 23, something remarkable happens. The light softens. The air warms. People slow down — and they show up for one another.

Golden Hour Unboxed is a free, cross-cultural evening at Bellevue Botanical Garden where Black entrepreneurs, artists, families, and allies gather under the sunset to mingle, share, and rise together. It's a celebration of the many ways our community contributes to the Eastside — through art, food, storytelling, mentorship, and the everyday brilliance of building something from nothing.

This is more than an event. It's a platform — for emerging Black entrepreneurs to mingle with seasoned professionals. For families to experience cross-cultural exchange in real time. For artists, vendors, and community builders to be seen and supported.

Plan Your Visit

Find your way through the garden.

Golden Hour Unboxed is held at the Aaron Education Center inside Bellevue Botanical Garden — 12001 Main St, Bellevue, WA. Enter at the Garden Entrance by the parking lot; the Education Center is a short, accessible walk just past the entrance. Explore the full garden map and accessible routes below.

Come early and walk the garden. The Bellevue Botanical Garden is open to the public all afternoon — arrive whenever the light calls you, wander the pathways, and make an evening of it. The Aaron Education Center doors open at 5:30 PM for check-in; program begins at 6:00 PM.

Open Garden Map (PDF) →

Map & access guide courtesy of Bellevue Botanical Garden.

What to Expect

An evening, five movements.

Programming designed for cross-generational connection — performances, ideas, and warmth that move from afternoon light into twilight.

i.

Sunset Sounds

Acoustic music, spoken word, and movement from cross-cultural artists — programmed for the garden's evening rhythm.

ii.

Storytelling

Personal narratives of building, belonging, and rising — voices from across the Eastside.

iii.

Micro Speed Pitching

Emerging entrepreneurs and artists share ideas shaped by their identities. Three minutes. One spotlight.

iv.

Pack-the-Box Drive

A back-to-school giving initiative powered by an upcoming nonprofit partnership. Bring supplies, leave with new friends.

v.

Twilight Social

As the sky turns lavender and gold, we gather for an unhurried social that closes the evening with warmth.

Storytellers for the Convening

The voices we'll gather around.

A small circle of founders, makers, and builders we have invited to carry their stories into the evening.

Each Storyteller for the Convening wears a corsage at the event. Look for the corsage and you have found someone with a story worth a moment of your time — about how they started, what they have built, and what they are still becoming. Stories happen on a walk through the garden, in conversation in the crowd, or briefly on stage as the sun softens.

Storyteller · Confirmed
Chezik Tsunoda
Founder & Executive Director · No More Under

Filmmaker, mother, and water-safety advocate. Founded No More Under after losing her three-year-old son Yori — turning unimaginable grief into a national mission that brings free swim lessons to Black and brown children, who drown at four to five times the rate of their peers. Her acclaimed documentary Drowning in Silence carries that work into theaters.

cheziktsunoda.com →

Get involved

Take the stage.

Three ways to get involved with Golden Hour — an open-mic pitch showcase for Black entrepreneurs, a call for artists to perform, and a hand behind the scenes as a volunteer. All vendor, speaker, and performer applications close Monday, July 20. Earlier submissions get first look.

For Entrepreneurs

Pitch your idea.

Black entrepreneurs — apply to pitch at Golden Hour's Micro Speed Pitching Showcase. A short window on the mic to share what you're building, in front of a live audience and a panel of judges. Emerging and established founders welcome. This same form is also how you sign up to be a Storyteller — indicate your role in the form.

Why This Event

Bellevue is one of Washington's most diverse cities. Intentional spaces for Black entrepreneurs to be celebrated and seen by their neighbors are still rare on the Eastside.

Golden Hour Unboxed is a free, public evening built to close that gap — for Black entrepreneurs, their families, and the whole Eastside community that gathers around them.

We hold this gathering in August, during National Black Business Month, because the timing matters. We hold it at Bellevue Botanical Garden because the place matters. We hold it as part of the City of Bellevue's Cross-Cultural Center without Walls because the structure of belonging matters.

This isn't a passive cultural showcase. It's an active exchange — Black entrepreneurs, allies, and neighbors sharing names, ideas, and how to find each other after the sun sets.

FAQ

Questions, answered.

Still curious? Email katoya@toyboxconsulting.net and we'll get back to you.

Golden Hour Unboxed is free to the public per our agreement with Bellevue Botanical Garden. RSVP secures your spot but does not include a charge. Please RSVP so we can plan accordingly for refreshments and seating.
Yes — please do! Bellevue Botanical Garden is open to the public all afternoon and is a beautiful place to wander. Arrive whenever you like, take in the pathways and plantings, and make an evening of it. The Aaron Education Center doors open at 5:30 PM for Golden Hour Unboxed check-in; the program begins at 6:00 PM.
Yes — all ages are welcome. Programming is designed for cross-generational engagement, and families are encouraged to attend together.
Golden Hour Unboxed is designed as an unhurried, flowing evening at Bellevue Botanical Garden's education facility — most guests stand, stroll, and mingle their way through the program. Tables are set up for vendors, food, and the Micro Speed Pitching Showcase. Accessibility seating is available throughout the evening for anyone who needs it. If you'd like to request accessibility accommodations in advance, email katoya@toyboxconsulting.net.
Because we are in peak summer season at the Bellevue Botanical Garden, we have reserved overflow parking for our guests at Wilburton Instructional Service Center (WISC) · 12241 Main St, Bellevue WA 98005 — a short walk east of the Garden along Main St. Look for Golden Hour Unboxed signage as you arrive. Build a few extra minutes into your arrival window to make the walk over comfortably. Carpooling and rideshare are still encouraged.
Yes. Bellevue Botanical Garden has accessible pathways and seating areas. If you have specific accessibility needs, please reach out to katoya@toyboxconsulting.net in advance and we'll make arrangements to support your visit.
Apply through our Pitch & Storyteller sign-up form. The same form is used for both formal Micro Speed Pitching slots and general Storyteller sign-ups — indicate which role you want inside the form.
Vendor tabling applications closed on July 20 and all tables are booked. If you missed the deadline, you can still join us as a Storyteller — you will get a nametag or identifier and can network and share your business throughout the evening. Sign up through our Pitch & Storyteller form.
We welcome partnership conversations at any level. Whether you're interested in being a presenting partner, programming sponsor, community supporter, in-kind contributor, or media partner — we'd love to design something together. Reach out to katoya@toyboxconsulting.net for our sponsor & partner outreach kit.
The event is hosted in partnership with Bellevue Botanical Garden, which has covered options. The date is firm: Sunday, August 23, 2026. Weather adjustments to programming (covered staging, etc.) will be communicated via email and social media leading up to the event.
Garden casual — think effortless evening wear. Layers are recommended as the temperature can shift from the warm afternoon into a cooler twilight. Shoes you can stand and stroll in, since most of the evening is spent on your feet. The botanical setting invites a celebratory, culturally expressive aesthetic — wear what makes you feel beautiful and yourself.
